explanation: Architect Alfred Butts tallied letters in the 1930s, so common letters such as E score 1 point and rare ones such as Q score 10.

claims.text: In the 1930s Alfred Butts, the inventor of Scrabble, set its letter values and tile counts from a frequency analysis of letters in printed sources, including The New York Times.
In English-language Scrabble, E is worth 1 point and Q is worth 10.
